items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: T-Bar, uh, Barbarin. That's the band we had.

ctx.x: Well, in that time, you see, that was hard and usually. You see, you get a band, you take a link to a day like on a Sunday, or you catch every

band in town. You see, to have work, you have to have a band, you have to have a band, and you have to have a band. But on the Sundays, you catch them big clubs, they get on out there and they watch for the bands. They get to have their band. They get to have their band. They get to have their band. They get out there and they watch, stand up and watch what band's coming along. The band gets the hot with you on one number, it's carrying your numbers. Well what you do, you go back and what you call the Red Bull,…
What else? He was playing clarinet. Clarinet. True clarinet.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-08-22
items.q: I see, Paul had went off, and after he come back he was different, but when he started out, he started out with us.

ctx.x: Yeah, I worked with every good man they had, and every bad man they had. Man, I didn't care who I worked with, long as I was working. Yeah, that's right. That's right. Some man, some man picked their man to work with them. Well, you take a man like Paul Barber and see, Paul Barber and he's a man. Yeah. He wasn't even anybody with him. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. I see, Paul had went off, and after he come back he was different, but when he started out, he started out with us. Oh, yeah. That's who he started with.
You say when he came back he was different. In what way he had?
